issues.message: all dielectric(s) ['substrate'] are perfectly lossless in an open (CPML) domain. If you are measuring Q / resonance, this gives an ARTIFICIALLY infinite Q (design-guide Anti-Pattern #1, an R5 surface-metric trap) — add loss, e.g. sigma = 2*pi*f*eps0*eps_r*tan_delta. (Harmless if you are not measuring Q.)

1 conductor sheet dimension(s) are solved more than 1% off their drawn size (worst 1 listed): geometry[1] 'pec' y: drawn 4mm, nodes cover 4mm, solved as 4.7mm (+17.50%). OBSERVED: the node span the sheet's realized footprint covers on this run's grid, plus 0.35 of the adjacent cell at each free in-plane edge -- a PEC sheet's edge is solved that far beyond its last node (measured on this solver, both polarizations; a flat wall has no such offset). REMEDY: build the in-plane profiles with rfx.mesh_edges.edge_aware_profiles(domain, dx, sheets=[...], solids=[...]) and pass them as Simulation(dx_profile=..., dy_profile=...); a node ON the edge is not the fix. STALE IF: the footprint's node span on the run's node coordinates does not reproduce the printed numbers.

1 conductor-Box design edge(s) sit off-lattice by more than 0.5% of their extent (worst 1 listed): geometry[1] 'pec' (sheet) y: extent 4mm, worst face residual 350µm (8.75% of the extent). OBSERVED: distance from each declared face to its nearest E-node on this run's own node coordinates; a PEC volume's face realizes on the nearest node plane and a sheet footprint on the nodes it covers (lattice ownership contract #931 §1.1/§1.3). Reported residuals describe declared-face alignment only. A sheet's extent can change by more than this nearest-node residual, and an extent change involves both faces. Read the realized bounds from fidelity_report(); frequency sensitivity depends on the mode and the affected dimension. COST (measured, #703): a uniform-mesh sweep rounded ONE substrate thickness by 8-10% across three 'convergence' points — three different boards solved under one name; the same campaign's board survived at dx=50um only because every patterned dimension happened to be an exact multiple of 50um. REMEDY: for a PEC VOLUME choose dx commensurate with its dimensions, slide the lattice origin onto the worst face, or (non-uniform lane) place mesh nodes on its faces; for a SHEET see sheet_effective_size -- a node on a sheet's edge is not the fix. COVERAGE: examined 4 axis extent(s) on 2 conductor Box declaration(s) on the uniform lane; 2 sheet normal axis/axes reported by sheet_plane_realized instead; 0 non-Box conductor entr(y/ies) skipped (no analytic face coordinates). STALE IF: |face - nearest node| on the run's node coordinates does not reproduce the printed residuals.

MSL port 'checked': declared trace at z=0.011 m maps to node 11 (z=0.011 m), but no longitudinal conductor edge meets it at width node 10. Observed conductor planes on this column are [0.006, 0.01] m. Make the port ground/trace declarations agree with the realized conductor surfaces. The conductor-plane gap is unavailable.

MSL port 'checked' at x=8.00mm, direction='+x': distance to nearest x-CPML = 8000µm (domain edge + 0mm calibrated CPML buffer) < recommended 10000µm (= 2·h_sub). Source-side CPML reflection may inflate |S11|. Move port further from boundary OR increase domain x-extent.

MSL port 'checked' (direction='+x'): the 5-probe ladder (n_probe_offset=25, n_probe_spacing=2 cells) runs past the grid and CLAMPS — only 1 of 5 probes land on distinct grid cells (4 duplicate probe position(s): (24.0, 24.0, 24.0, 24.0, 24.0)mm). The N-probe least-squares wave-decomposition fit is rank-deficient on duplicated positions; `compute_msl_s_matrix`'s Z0/S11 extraction is unreliable for this port. Shorten n_probe_offset/n_probe_spacing or extend the domain so the full ladder stays in-grid.
